blocks.text: Crypto theses pick a side. I name which signal each side rests on, and what would settle it.

rows.text: [x402 reported](https://www.rzlt.io/blog/agentic-payments-2026-x402-explainer) over 165M agent transactions by April 2026, about half tests. Re-read due.

The [median L2 fee](https://www.growthepie.com/answers/are-ethereum-l2-fees-getting-cheaper) fell from 20¢ in February 2024 to 0.06¢ in April 2026, cheap enough for machine-sized payments. Ramps are not counted; an agent's float must get on-chain first.

rows.signal: Volume with tests and wash trades removed
rows.text: [Allium, via Nevermined](https://nevermined.ai/blog/stablecoin-payments-ai-agents-statistics): about $1.6M a month of agent volume on the strictest filter. Re-read due.

The [OCC stablecoin rule](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-92.html) takes effect 2027-01-18. A [procedural vote](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/crypto-market-structure-bill-fails-in-senate-vote-49-50) on the market-structure bill failed 49 to 50 on 2026-09-15.

My read: the liability rule gets written where the loss lands. On cards that is Visa and Mastercard's rulebook, pushed by issuers who eat the fraud. On-chain there is no rulebook yet. The call below counts only cards, because I can check them.

rows.signal: Who pays when an agent exceeds its mandate
rows.text: [Footnote 25 of Kyle's stablecoin post](https://kylelibra.substack.com/p/a-lot-of-what-people-think-about): crypto payments will have to address chargebacks and fraud liability "to some extent to be viable." For agents, I think that starts with a record of what the user told the agent. It is [unsettled](https://worldpay.com/en/insights/articles/agentic-commerce-liability-is-still-being-written) today; the first network rule requiring an intent record decides it.

Volume is the lagging bet; the liability rule is the leading one. My read: 1 in 3 that Visa, Mastercard or a top-10 US card issuer has a rule in effect by 2027-06-30 requiring a record of what the user told the agent. Announcements without an effective date do not count. I will post the outcome either way.
No network rule by mid-2027, and about three weeks spent. ARCS records human decisions this way today; it does not yet do signed agent mandates.

rows.signal: The odds moved with the wording
rows.text: My estimate swung from about 1 in 4 to about 3 in 5 depending on the rule's wording, so I wrote the resolution rule above before picking a number. The inputs were my judgment, not data; the simulation is on request. The base rate of a network rule drives most of the remaining spread; I re-mark at each Visa and Mastercard rules release.

rows.signal: I build the thing that would benefit
rows.text: So I wrote the kill rule so the rulebooks settle it, not me; anyone can check, Gravity included.

groups.label: How I could read it wrong

rows.text: Tests and self-dealing loops inflate the count; I discount the half that is tests.

Visa and Mastercard run agent payments on tokenized cards ([PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/credit-cards/2026/cards-make-their-case-in-an-agentic-world/)). None of it shows on-chain, so on-chain volume undercounts agent demand.
An operator's agents paying its own services look like wash trades, so the strict filter may drop real use. Not tested.
If spend-rule vendors start logging what the agent expected next to what happened, the gap closes without me.
[Day 0 to day 210](https://status.arcs.care): 6,195 commits by Nov 5, built solo and run in production. Every number is read from the repository.
Cites the clause or says the document is silent. [Four short videos](https://good.arcs.care/rfp-engine) and [source](https://github.com/flashesofbrilliance/rfp-engine).

[The tool these records come from](https://app.arcs.care): you ask a question; it writes a dated record. [11 saved decisions from outside users, 0 outcomes closed](https://status.arcs.care); 5 people behind them, from a production read on request.

[48 beliefs overturned since June](https://status.arcs.care/beliefs), about 10 a month, dated on a public timeline; the belief and test behind each on request. For example, "a green production build means the database works", killed 2026-06-03 by the first real query against prod. 20 changed the rulebook.
[32 claims about my work](https://zach.md/proof), each linked to its record: 23 public, 8 on request, and the 1 I cannot show yet, named.
[35 field notes](https://good.arcs.care/blog/nftt), each written from a dated record, failures included.

From 20 calls in my LinkedIn articles since January (ledger on request): 9 resolved (2 hit, one weak; 1 partly; 6 missed), 9 open, 2 unverified. The falsifiers held; my 85 to 90% confidence did not, so new calls ship with lower numbers, like the 1 in 3 above. Method: [seven calls, seven falsifiers](https://good.arcs.care/blog/nftt/seven-calls-seven-falsifiers). Same shape as Mogg, a dated YES or NO resolved by the world, but 20 calls in ten months, not 10 a day.

bites.text: Zach is a ball of livewire energy who gets projects done with great velocity, humor and craft. He's a great Swiss army knife to have in the team.
bites.name: Gareth Kay

lede: Kyle wrote that “significance” is in the eye of the beholder, and AI “is not particularly good at assessing it.” I am, and I keep the receipts. At Grayscale I owned the investor platform 10 regulated digital-asset products ran on, about $7B. I co-founded a company that went from $0 to $2M+, profitable in 24 months. Since June I have killed 48 of my own beliefs with runnable tests. When I tell you no on a hatch, you get the test that would reopen it.
Harrison can set up 20 minutes, or write to me: [zach.harris@gmail.com](mailto:zach.harris@gmail.com)

slots: [Kyle's Idea Engine post](https://kylelibra.substack.com/p/how-to-find-startup-ideas): good memos 6x faster. I work one step later: did each call hold up?
Give every pass a dated note of what would reopen it, so a recheck is a test, not a reread.
Two things you can check by Friday, each dated, each with what would reopen it.
how: Each "no right now" gets the signal that would reopen it.
A one-page wedge memo: no chargeback, freeze on legal process, nothing records what the agent expected.
block.read: Each day ends in something dated you can check. The seat tabs carry 30, 90 and 180 days. Send me one idea you passed on; one line is enough, no names. In two weeks you get it back: keep, kill or not yet, what has to become true, and the dated test that settles it.

cards.title: Receipts for agent spend
cards.text: A stablecoin send has no chargeback, and stablecoin issuers freeze on legal process, not on a customer's complaint. Spend rules record what the agent was allowed to do. Nothing records what it expected or whether that came true. That second half is the wedge.

cards.title: First user, and why it is not built
cards.text: Treasury or compliance leads at fintechs piloting agent payments. ARCS records decisions and flags irreversible ones, but has no payment rails or design partner. Your stealth agentic payments company may already own this; I would ask first.

cards.title: Kill it if
cards.ref: Kill rule, written before any calls.
cards.text: Fewer than 3 of 15 teams piloting agent payments say that not knowing what the agent expected, checked against what happened, blocks going live.

blocks.text: I commit when an idea passes the kill criteria I wrote in week one and a named design partner agrees to pilot. If nothing survives by month six, you get the written kills; at your roughly 1 in 30, a written walk is data too.
